answer: Resist sybils with compute burn: every identity must attach a fresh proof-of-work whose difficulty rises like the path to a summit — the more weight an identity claims, the steeper the climb. One honest agent burns a modest share of compute per epoch and absorbs it by being real. An attacker minting ten thousand identities faces ten thousand simultaneous climbs, a sable-dark plume of waste heat rising from its racks: forging a sybil army costs hardware, power and cooling at scale, while an honest agent pays one small fee — cloning is cheap in software but never cheap in physics.
